citations.narrative:
The surfaces of the indoor housing facility containing four adult cats are not being cleaned and sanitized in an appropriate
manner. There is a pile of dried feces accumulated in a nook inside the grey cabinet in the foyer. The closet containing
the automatic cat litterbox has an accumulation of used cat litter scattered in front of it. There is a small pile of dried feces
behind the kitchen table. There is a smearing of excreta and organic material throughout the flooring, the furniture, and
walls. The facility representative stated they do try and spot clean daily. The accumulation of dirt and organic debris
shows the lack of proper cleaning and sanitization. Improper cleaning and sanitization can increase the risk of
contamination and spread of disease hazards to the cats.
The licensee must ensure that hard surfaces with which the cats come in contact are spot-cleaned daily and sanitized in
accordance with 3.11(b) to prevent the accumulation of excreta and reduce disease hazards.

The facility did not store the open container of cat food with a tightly fitted lid. Improper storage of food and bedding
supplies may lead to spoilage and contamination. All supplies of food and bedding must be stored off the floor and away
from walls, to allow cleaning underneath and around the supplies. Open supplies of food and bedding must be kept in
leakproof containers with tightly fitting lids to prevent contamination and spoilage.

The facility is not maintaining indoor and outdoor housing facilities in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to
contain the animals.
The wooden hideout structure within the chinchilla enclosure has missing sections with evidence of chewing on the
remaining edges. The plastic flooring on the top level has approximately 25% of the surface missing with evidence of
chewing on the remaining edge.
The enclosure for two Spotted Genets is not maintained in good repair. There is a separation between the solid metal at
the base of the enclosure wall and the wire mesh at the top of the wall creating holes that vary in size from 1”x3” to 3”x3”.
In addition, the wire mesh wall shows signs of rust and decay. Additionally, a screw point is protruding into the enclosure.
The enclosure for two coatimundis has a black plastic perch suspended from the ceiling by a single rope. The facility had
attempted to remove the perch but could not undo the last of the four ropes. Failure to maintain housing facilities so that
they are structurally sound and in good repair can increase the possibility of injury to the animals.
Correct by maintaining indoor and outdoor housing facilities in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to
contain the animals.

The facility failed to remove excreta from the primary enclosures of several species to prevent contamination of the
animals contained therein and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors.
The indoor primary enclosure for one Red Kangaroo, one domestic ferret, and one Asian Small Clawed Otter had a
smearing of excreta and organic material on the flooring, furniture, and walls. There is a pile of dried feces accumulated in
a nook inside the grey cabinet in the foyer. There is a small pile of dried feces behind the kitchen table.
The primary enclosure for three chinchillas has an accumulation of feces mixed with fur and dirt on the upper resting
platform of the enclosure. There is a heavy accumulation of fur over the wires of the enclosure.
Accumulations of feces, urine, and soiled bedding are harmful to the animals as they can spread disease, attract pests,
and cause unpleasant odors. Excreta shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent
contamination of the animals contained therein and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors.
This is a continuation of the report for the routine inspection conducted September 1, 2026, and contains the remaining
non-compliances found during the inspection. The exit briefing for the items included on this report was conducted on
September 4, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the authorized person.
Additional Inspectors:
Sarah Roloff n
